root_cause.text: The workqueue type was prematurely set to NONE before its resources (descriptors, completions, sbitmap) were freed, causing subsequent cleanup to be skipped and resulting in a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `wq->type = IDXD_WQT_NONE;` from `idxd_wq_disable_cleanup()` and `idxd_drv_disable_wq()` into `idxd_wq_free_resources()`, ensuring the type is set only after resources are released. The CVE description states that setting type to NONE "means that the wq is empty (all its resources were released)" and that it should be set only after resources are released.

The CVE description states that setting type to NONE "means that the wq is empty (all its resources were released)" and that it should be set only after resources are released.

candidates.rationale: This statement prematurely sets the workqueue type to NONE before its resources (descriptors, completions, sbitmap) are freed. As a result, subsequent cleanup functions may skip freeing these resources due to a check on the type, causing a memory leak.
This call invokes the reset function which contains the premature assignment of wq->type to NONE. It is part of the path that leads to the type being set before resource freeing occurs.

This statement sets the workqueue state to DISABLED as part of the reset. It may interact with conditional checks that determine whether resources should be freed, contributing to the skipping of cleanup.
This statement clears the workqueue configuration, which is part of the premature reset. It may affect logic that triggers resource deallocation, compounding the vulnerability.
This redundant assignment after resource freeing does not directly cause the leak, but it is another place where the type is set to NONE and may override any later checks, making cleanup ineffective.
